quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #4
										  					
  

40 Questions • Passing Score 32

questions.question: When turning or changing lanes, you must:

options.text: Always signal, even if you don't see any other cars.
Signal only if other cars are nearby.
Signal only when driving at night.
Signal only in heavy traffic at night.

questions.correctAnswerText: Always signal, even if you don't see any other cars.
questions.explanation: Always signal when you change lanes, turn, or leave the curb. Make this a habit so you don't forget.

questions.question: To drive safely at night, you should:

options.text: Stay farther away from the car in front of you.
Don't drive if you are tired.
Make sure your headlights work properly.
All of the above.

questions.explanation: At night, you can't see as well. Take these steps to keep yourself and other drivers safe in the dark.

questions.question: When you see a flashing yellow light, you should:

options.text: Speed up.
Stop completely.
Turn on your headlights.
Slow down and be careful.

questions.explanation: A flashing yellow light warns you of danger ahead. Slow down and proceed with caution.

questions.question: To make sure your health doesn't affect your driving, you should:

options.text: Stay in good physical shape and get regular checkups.
Know how your medicines affect your driving.
Drive only within what you can safely handle.
All of the above.

questions.explanation: Your health is important for safe driving. Know your limits and only drive when it is safe to do so.

questions.question: A driver entering a public road from a driveway or private road:

options.text: Has the right-of-way.
Must let cars on the public road go first.
Can push into traffic.
Can expect other drivers to move for you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Must let cars on the public road go first.
questions.explanation: When entering traffic from a driveway or private road, let the cars on the public road pass first. Merge safely when you have a clear opening.

questions.question: Before changing lanes, you should:

options.text: Check your side mirror.
Check your rearview mirror.
Turn your head quickly to look for other cars.
All of the above.

questions.explanation: Check both mirrors to see traffic behind you. Just before moving to the other lane, quickly look over your shoulder to check for cars in your blind spot.

questions.question: Before you start the car, you should:

options.text: Make sure only back passengers have buckled up.
Make sure only adult passengers have buckled up.
Make sure only children have buckled up.
Make sure all passengers have buckled up.

questions.correctAnswerText: Make sure all passengers have buckled up.
questions.explanation: Before you start driving, buckle your seatbelt and make sure everyone in the car does too. Make this part of your routine.

questions.question: Always signal when:

options.text: Changing lanes.
Parking or leaving a parking space.
Entering traffic from an alley or parking lot.
All of the above.

questions.explanation: Always use your turn signal for these situations. Let other drivers know what you are doing to prevent accidents.

questions.question: When you see a red traffic light, you should:

options.text: Drive through if no other cars are coming.
Keep driving because you have the right-of-way.
Stop only if a police officer is watching.
Stop completely.

questions.explanation: A red light means stop. Running a red light is illegal and very dangerous. You may turn right on red only if a sign says you can.

questions.question: When you see angry drivers around you, you should:

options.text: Don't look at them.
Don't make hand gestures.
Get away from the situation.
All of these.

questions.explanation: When drivers are angry, stay away from them. Don't look at them or make gestures. Slow down, move over, or do whatever keeps you safe.

questions.question: When stopped for a traffic violation or equipment check, what must the driver show?

options.text: Proof of insurance.
A driver's license.
Proof of registration.
All of the above.

questions.explanation: When stopped by police, you must show your driver's license, proof of registration, and proof of insurance. All three documents must be in your vehicle when you drive.

questions.question: Alcohol is the leading cause of fatal car crashes.

options.text: True
False

questions.explanation: Alcohol is the number one cause of deadly car crashes. It hurts your vision and slows your reaction time, making it harder to respond to emergencies. Even small amounts of alcohol affect your driving.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Stop.
No U-turn.
Yield.
Do not enter.

questions.explanation: This sign is placed at the start of one-way streets and ramps. It tells you that you cannot drive in that direction.

questions.question: Who must use seat belts?

options.text: Only the driver.
Only adult passengers.
Only child passengers.
Everyone in the vehicle.

questions.explanation: All people in a vehicle must use seat belts. Make sure seat belts are clean, working properly, and available to everyone. Minnesota law requires vehicles to have seat belts and everyone must use them.

questions.question: How do you check your blind spot before changing lanes?

options.text: Look in the left side mirror.
Look in the right side mirror.
Look in the rearview mirror.
Look over your shoulder toward where you want to move.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look over your shoulder toward where you want to move.
questions.explanation: Before changing lanes, turn your head and look over your shoulder in the direction you plan to move. This helps you see areas that mirrors cannot show.

questions.question: Why should you not follow other cars too closely?

options.text: You may not see the road between the cars.
You may not have time to stop if the car ahead slows or stops suddenly.
You may not see the car's turn signals.
You may not see the car's brake lights.

questions.correctAnswerText: You may not have time to stop if the car ahead slows or stops suddenly.
questions.explanation: If you follow too closely and the car in front stops suddenly, you will not have enough time to stop. This can cause a crash.

questions.question: Must you always stop for a stopped school bus on a two-lane road?

options.text: True
False

questions.explanation: You must always stop for a stopped school bus on a two-lane road, no matter which direction you are driving. Be careful around children.

questions.question: At a four-way stop, who has the right-of-way?

options.text: The driver who arrives first.
The driver who arrives last.
One driver should go without stopping.
One driver should wave the others ahead.

questions.explanation: All four drivers must stop at a four-way stop. The driver who arrives first goes first. If two drivers arrive at the same time, the one on the right goes first.

questions.question: Where can you make a U-turn?

options.text: On a freeway.
Near the top of a hill.
In the middle of a curve.
Where it will not disrupt traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: Where it will not disrupt traffic.
questions.explanation: A U-turn is a 180-degree turn that reverses your direction. You can only make a U-turn if it is safe and does not interfere with other drivers.

questions.question: A pedestrian starts to cross in front of your car. What should you do?

options.text: Flash your lights.
Slow down.
Speed up and drive in front of the pedestrian.
Stop and let the pedestrian cross.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop and let the pedestrian cross.
questions.explanation: Slow down and be ready to stop whenever you see pedestrians on the road. Be extra careful around children. Always let pedestrians cross in a crosswalk.

questions.question: Which statement is true?

options.text: Sudden weather changes require you to change how you drive.
You should slow down when driving in rain and fog.
Watch for vehicles coming up behind you in bad weather.
All of the above.

questions.explanation: When weather changes suddenly, you must adjust your driving. Slow down in rain and fog. Watch for vehicles behind you that may be driving too fast for the conditions.

questions.question: When an emergency vehicle with sirens and flashing lights approaches you, you should pull to the right edge of the road and let it pass.

options.text: True
False

questions.explanation: When an emergency vehicle with lights and/or sirens approaches you, pull to the right side of the road immediately and let it pass.

questions.question: You are borrowing an unfamiliar vehicle from a friend. You should:

options.text: Not worry about it because all vehicles are the same.
Not tell your friend you are unfamiliar with the vehicle.
Ignore any obvious problems to avoid embarrassing your friend.
Take a few minutes to learn where everything is and how it works before you drive.

questions.correctAnswerText: Take a few minutes to learn where everything is and how it works before you drive.
questions.explanation: Before driving an unfamiliar vehicle, take time to find the turn signals, hazard lights, headlights, windshield wipers, brakes, gear selector, and horn. Fix any problems before driving.

questions.question: At night, what is hardest to see?

options.text: Road signs.
Pedestrians.
Other drivers.
Street lights.

questions.explanation: Pedestrians are harder to see at night than signs and other roadside objects.

questions.question: A yellow and black diamond-shaped sign means:

options.text: There are dangerous conditions on or near the road.
It helps direct you to cities and towns ahead.
It tells you about traffic laws and rules.
It tells you about road construction ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: There are dangerous conditions on or near the road.
questions.explanation: Warning signs tell you about dangerous conditions on or near the road ahead. They are diamond-shaped with black symbols or words on a yellow background.

questions.question: On a long trip, what helps prevent fatigue?

options.text: Stop and rest every two hours.
Do arm exercises every hour.
Drive with one eye open at a time.
Change feet on the gas pedal.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop and rest every two hours.
questions.explanation: Stop every two hours for a short break on long trips. If you feel sleepy, pull over to a safe place and nap or find a place to sleep.

questions.question: What affects braking distance?

options.text: How fast your vehicle is going.
The condition of your brakes and tires.
The condition of the road surface.
All of the above.

questions.explanation: Braking distance depends on your vehicle's speed, the condition of your brakes and tires, and the condition of the road surface.

questions.question: Drinking alcohol while taking drugs can:

options.text: Reduce the effects of drugs and alcohol.
Increase the effects of both drugs and alcohol.
Help cure your illness.
Improve your driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Increase the effects of both drugs and alcohol.
questions.explanation: Mixing alcohol and drugs can increase the effects of both. Driving after alcohol or drugs is unsafe. Mixing them is even more dangerous.

questions.question: This sign means:

options.text: One-way traffic.
Intersection ahead.
Traffic merging from the right.
Highway curves ahead.

questions.explanation: This sign warns you that traffic will merge into your lane from the right.

questions.question: The faster you drive, the longer it takes to stop when other drivers make unexpected moves.

options.text: TRUE
FALSE

questions.explanation: The faster you drive, the longer it takes to stop when you need to react to other drivers' unexpected moves.

questions.question: What are the most effective safety restraints in a traffic crash?

options.text: Only a lap and shoulder belt.
Only an airbag.
Both a lap/shoulder belt and an airbag.
No safety restraints.

questions.correctAnswerText: Both a lap/shoulder belt and an airbag.
questions.explanation: Safety belts double your chance of surviving a crash and more than double your chance of avoiding serious injury. Airbags work best with safety belts and give extra protection in front-end crashes. Always wear both shoulder and lap belts.

questions.question: If a police officer is directing traffic at a working traffic light, what should drivers do?

options.text: Follow the directions indicated by the traffic light.
Follow the directions given by the officer.
Honk at the officer.
Check to see what the cars next to them are doing.

questions.correctAnswerText: Follow the directions given by the officer.
questions.explanation: Traffic signals control traffic and prevent crashes. Drivers, pedestrians, and cyclists must obey traffic signals. However, when a police officer is directing traffic, you must follow the officer's directions instead.

questions.question: If an approaching train is close or fast enough to be dangerous, what must you do?

options.text: Slow down and proceed with caution.
Not cross the tracks until the train has completely passed.
Cross the tracks at your own risk.
Find an alternative route across tracks.

questions.correctAnswerText: Not cross the tracks until the train has completely passed.
questions.explanation: Look and listen for trains before crossing any railroad tracks. If a train is near or going fast enough to be dangerous, do not cross the tracks. This is true even if there are no signals or if the signals are broken.

questions.question: What lane width are motorcycles entitled to?

options.text: The bicycle lane.
The same full lane width as other motor vehicles.
Half the width of a lane.
The width of the sidewalk.

questions.correctAnswerText: The same full lane width as other motor vehicles.
questions.explanation: Motorcyclists need the full lane width to stay safe. Motorcycles have the right to use the same full lane width as all other vehicles.

questions.question: Drivers are not required to yield to pedestrians in a crosswalk. True or false?

options.text: True
False

questions.explanation: Drivers must stop and yield when a pedestrian is in a marked crosswalk. Drivers must also yield to pedestrians in unmarked crosswalks on the driver's side when there are no traffic signals.

questions.question: Is it wise to continually improve your driving and observation skills because driving involves risk?

options.text: True
False

questions.explanation: Driving becomes unsafe if you think you have nothing to learn. Always work to improve your driving and observation skills for your safety and the safety of others.

questions.question: When you are in a travel lane on the roadway, what should you do?

options.text: You may stop to drop off passengers.
You may stop to look up an address.
You may make a U-turn or back up if you get on the wrong entrance ramp of the freeway.
Don't stop for any reason. Keep moving until you can safely pull off the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Don't stop for any reason. Keep moving until you can safely pull off the road.
questions.explanation: Never stop in a travel lane. Keep moving until you can safely pull off the road. If you miss your turn or exit, do not back up. Go to the next turn or exit where you can safely turn around.

questions.question: What should you do before turning?

options.text: Use your signal.
Turn the wheel.
Increase your speed.
Change lanes.

questions.explanation: To turn safely, turn on your signal three to four seconds before you turn.

questions.question: How can you avoid being in a truck or bus driver's blind spot?

options.text: Never pass them.
Avoid driving alongside them and avoid tailgating.
Flash your lights at them.
Sound your horn.

questions.correctAnswerText: Avoid driving alongside them and avoid tailgating.
questions.explanation: Large vehicles like trucks and buses have large blind spots on the sides and rear. Do not drive alongside them and do not tailgate them.

questions.question: You feel angry after an incident at work. When you get to your car, what should you do?

options.text: Play the radio loudly so you won't think about it.
Drive fast on the interstate to let off steam.
Take a few minutes to cool off before you begin your drive home.
Stop at your favorite bar and have a few drinks before driving home.

questions.correctAnswerText: Take a few minutes to cool off before you begin your drive home.
questions.explanation: If you are upset, angry, or distracted by emotions, take time to calm down before driving. Letting out anger while driving is dangerous for you and others on the road.
